ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, rod AB rotates clockwise in a vertical plane about point A with constant angular velocity ω, and drives the small ring M sleeved on the fixed horizontal rod OC to move. The distance between A and O is h. At the beginning of the motion, rod AB is in the vertical position. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is a vertical support. A higher position on the support is marked O, and a lower position is marked A; from O to the right is a fixed horizontal rod OC. There is also an inclined rod AB with A as its endpoint, inclined upward to the right. At the intersection of inclined rod AB and horizontal rod OC there is a small ring M; therefore small ring M is sleeved on both AB and OC at the same time, and its position is the intersection point of the two rods, and it can only make horizontal motion along the horizontal rod OC. Then reason: Take A as the coordinate origin, vertically upward as the y-axis, and horizontally to the right as the x-axis. Because AO=h, the equation of the fixed horizontal rod OC is y=h. Rod AB starts from the vertical position and rotates about point A clockwise with uniform angular velocity. After time t, its angle with the vertical direction is θ=ωt. Any point on inclined rod AB satisfies x/y=tanθ, so the abscissa of its intersection point M with y=h is x_M=h tanθ=h tan(ωt). The small ring M moves along the horizontal rod, so the magnitude of its velocity is the derivative of the abscissa with respect to time: v=dx_M/dt=hω sec^2(ωt)=ωh/cos^2(ωt).
